# YellowBird

> Documentation for YellowBird, a Go media pipeline. An upload is stored, a job id is published on Redis, and a separate worker runs FFmpeg.

The docs live at https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs. The API origin is https://api.amaanworks.me. The Go module is https://github.com/dexisback/YellowBird. The workspace is a separate Next.js app. AWS is a separate Terraform repo.

Sitemap: https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs/sitemap-index.xml
Feed: https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs/rss.xml

## Docs

- [YellowBird docs](https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs): How the API, workspace, and cloud repos connect.
- [Run it locally](https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs/run): Postgres, Redis, the API, and the worker on one machine.
- [Architecture](https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs/architecture): The path of one upload, and what survives a Redis flush.
- [Backend](https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs/backend): Go processes, tables, Redis Streams, and FFmpeg flags.
- [Web](https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs/web): The Next.js workspace and the API origin it calls.
- [Ops and cloud](https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs/ops): ECS Fargate, S3, and which repo deploys images versus infrastructure.
- [API](https://yellowbird.amaanworks.me/docs/api): HTTP routes, JWT, and the multipart upload body.

There is no HLS playlist in the worker. A video upload creates a thumbnail, a 10 second preview, and H.264 MP4s at 360p, 720p, and 1080p.
